target_customer: Remote-first companies paying for scheduled virtual team-building events
problem: Distributed teams lacked social bonding and had no easy way to run engaging team events.
business_model: B2B subscription or per-event fee for hosted virtual team-building events

founders.name: Melissa Du
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; her profile there mentions Voltage Park, a later role.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists the company as Inactive and the domain now redirects to a domain name marketplace.

competitors.name: Confetti
competitors.what: Virtual team-building experiences such as escape quests, trivia and classes for remote teams

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling and video-call events with off-the-shelf tools; the work was content and hosting.

defensibility.rationale: Event content and hosting could be copied by other event firms in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many virtual event firms appeared during 2020. No incumbent bought Cadence.

market_need_then: The March 2020 move to remote work created sudden demand for remote team culture tools.

branding.domain_note: Used cadencework.com, a compound domain, since the .com is held by others. The domain now redirects to a name marketplace page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline 'Delightful team-building events for remote companies'

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found only unrelated companies named Cadence and a Kadence workplace firm; no press about this brand. The name is shared by many firms.

outcome_analysis: Cadence was a two person team that entered YC in Winter 2020 just as remote work surged, selling virtual team-building events. YC lists it Inactive and its domain now redirects to a domain marketplace, but no source states why it stopped, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: The 150K pre-seed is from Employbl (derived from Diffbot) alone and is probably the standard YC deal; undated. The redirect target atom.com was not fetched (a redirect to another host); the dead-site conclusion rests on the redirect to a name marketplace. Confetti source is dated Aug 2020, five months after the March 2020 batch, and mentions Confetti only in passing; competitor coverage is thin. A Product Hunt listing for Cadence Team-building Events exists (launch date reported as June 2022 by a Hunted page) and may or may not be the same company.
